title: A closed line shows the date it closed, not the invoice date
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance. Open the schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', or create it with New schedule: add service 'PM-A' with a Calendar trigger of Every 6 months and canned lines, for example 'Engine oil and filter change' 0.8 hours, 'Chassis lubrication, 12 points' 0.5 hours, 'Air filter inspection' 0.3 hours and 'Brake adjustment check' 1.2 hours (4 lines, 2.8 hours). Save.
  3. Open Customers, open customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' (create it if missing), open its Assets tab and open unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' (create it with New Asset if missing). Open the asset's Maintenance tab. If the unit is not on the schedule, press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', enter a last service date for PM-A about seven months ago (for example 6 Mar 2026) and press Enroll. PM-A now reads Overdue on the Maintenance tab.
  4. On the customer page press New Work Order, choose unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' and create the work order (it opens as an estimate). Note its number, for example S3780-15904.
  5. On the work order page, find the Maintenance schedule card inside the asset card at the top and press Expand.
  6. On the PM-A row press Add Service; in the Add PM-A to <work order number> window keep Add to this work order selected and press Add. The row now reads Added · 4 lines.
custom_steps:
1. On the Lines tab complete one PM-A line today and read that line.
  2. Leave the other PM-A lines open; read them.
  3. The next day (or later), complete the remaining PM-A lines, then open Finance and press Create Invoice; read the date proposed in When was the maintenance done? and the dates shown on the lines.
  4. Before invoicing, complete the work order (Complete work order) and watch for any maintenance step.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • A completed line shows the date it closed (in the older work-order board: Closed 4 Sep), labelled so it is not the invoice date.
  • A line that is still open shows no closed date.
  • After invoicing, each line keeps its own closed date, distinct from the invoice date, and the step proposes the day PM-A's lines were all closed.
  • Completing the work order shows no maintenance step; the step appears only after Create Invoice.
  • PM-A counts as completed only when every line it added is completed: the proposed date is the day the last of them closed.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10574 (S18, Complete a service and reset the cycle); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S18; Design MR_V2_2 (Claude Design export, 6 Oct 2026), driven in full on 6 Oct 2026, 4-work-order (old WO chrome) board, Lines tab; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R9: “Each closed line will stamp the date it closed, visible on the work order and distinct from the invoice date”
  • S18-R13: “The date proposed is when that service's own lines were all closed, which S18-R9 stamps, and the invoice date only where there is nothing better”
  • Design, 4-work-order (old WO chrome) board, Lines tab, completed PM-A line: “Closed 4 Sep”
  • S18-N6: “Completing a work order shows no maintenance step. Everything happens in the step after invoicing”
  • S18-R10: “A service added by its canned lines completes when every line it added completes”
